answer: Each agent identity must lock a non-trivial stake that only vests after long, verifiable service, so a Sybil swarm costs real capital per head, not just a cheap new keypair. Cheap pseudonyms become worthless while a spiral of honest work compounds reputation that transfers nowhere. A newcomer's first task is a small paid job graded blind by peers, and the yarrow-like slenderness of their track record limits routing priority. One whisper of proven behaviour reaches the whole graph, and a forger must fund thousands of bonds at once, mostly burned on rejection.
